title: Throughput price oscillation risk decomposition
content:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

This workbook explores how short-term oscillations in customer throughput (token/sec bursts and quiet tails) interact with our pricing bands and reserved capacity commitments to create asymmetric runway risk. The goal is to: (1) quantify marginal margin erosion across 5 throughput scenarios, (2) propose a headcount stitching plan to soften ops costs during oscillation periods, and (3) recommend soft price-band rules that reduce churn risk while preserving unit economics.

Key assumptions (base case):
- Base GTM ARR mix: 55% mid-market, 30% PLG, 15% enterprise.
- Average token price (hosted) base: $0.0007/token for gen; embeddings priced at $0.0008/unit equivalent.
- Dedicated reserved capacity cost (monthly amortized): $80k per pool (8 GPUs).
- Avg sustained throughput per pool: 12k tokens/sec (model mix weighted).
- Oscillation index (OI): standard deviation of observed 5-min qps divided by mean qps; base OI = 0.45.

SCENARIOS (5):
- S1: Low oscillation (OI 0.2), steady growth +8% q/q.
- S2: Moderate oscillation (OI 0.45), seasonal bursts (end of quarter peaks).
- S3: High oscillation (OI 0.8), frequent microbursts from new customers.
- S4: Constrained capacity (regional GPU pressure) causing 12% fallback to lower-cost variants.
- S5: Pricing compression shock (-18% realized token price due to competitor reprice).

SENSITIVITY GRID (example extract):
Columns = Scenario / Month 1-12. Rows show: tokens served (M), reserved pool count, burst spot spend ($), avg realized price ($/token), gross margin (%), headcount cost ($), net contribution ($).

Sample rows (Month 1 baseline):
- tokens_served: [120, 135, 150, 160, 155, 170, 180, 190, 210, 230, 250, 270] (in millions)
- reserved_pools: [10, 10, 11, 11, 11, 12, 12, 12, 13, 13, 14, 14]
- burst_spend: [$180k, $210k, $240k, $280k, $260k, $300k, $320k, $350k, $410k, $460k, $520k, $600k]
- avg_price: [$0.00070, $0.00070, $0.00069, $0.00069, $0.00068, $0.00068, $0.00067, $0.00067, $0.00066, $0.00066, $0.00065, $0.00064]
- gross_margin_pct: [62, 60, 58, 57, 55, 53, 52, 50, 48, 45, 42, 39]

HEADCOUNT STITCHING (proposal):
- Objective: Smooth fixed ops payroll with a mix of full-time SRE/infra hires + a rotating pool of contractors to absorb burst-day incident work and on-call intensity.
- Proposed FY29 phasing: hire 6 permanent infra/SRE FTEs in H1, hold 8 contractor FTE equiv as bench.
- Trigger rules (w/ hysteresis):
  * If 7-day rolling burst_spend > 1.4x baseline AND OI > 0.6 -> convert 2 contractors to perm hires (up to bench limit).
  * If 30-day burst_spend < 0.8x baseline AND reserved_pools utilization < 70% -> re-evaluate bench (pause contractor renewals).
- Cost math (simplified): perm_FTE fully loaded = $260k/yr; contractor bench weighted cost = $140k/yr equivalent.

PRICING BAND RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Introduce a small dynamic floor: for customers with >500M tokens/mo, apply a floor price that scales with committed reserved fraction to reduce realized-price variance.
- Soft-cap on promotional credits for accounts that generate >15% of total burst cost in a quarter.
- Offer an "Oscillation Smoothing" addon: +4% on list price in exchange for guaranteed buffer pool access and lower spot exposure.

RISK DECOMPOSITION (why oscillation harms margin):
1) Burst-driven spot GPU usage is billed at higher per-hour cloud rates and invalidates some reserved amortization assumptions.
2) Price erosion during open-market competitive events forces realized avg_price down faster than cost per token falls (cost stickiness).
3) Operational headcount must scale to incident volume, creating stepwise increases to fixed OPEX.

RUNWAY IMPACT METRIC (simple):
- Delta runway months = runway_base - (variable_burn_increase / avg_monthly_burn)
- Example S3 impact: variable_burn_increase (extra burst + contractor conversion) = $3.2M/quarter -> runway reduction ~ 1.9 months vs base.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs:
- Validate OI distribution on historical 5-min telemetry (ask infra/data team for sample 2027-2029 windows).
- Model cross-customer correlation: how many bursts are idiosyncratic vs system-wide? (affects pooling efficiency).
- Price elasticity calibration: need per-segment elasticity estimates (PLG vs enterprise). Suggested Jira: JIRA-FIN-2159.

APPENDIX (spreadsheet formulas and notes):
- burst_spend = max(0, observed_tokens_above_reserved_capacity * spot_rate_per_token)
- effective_reserved_unit_cost = reserved_pool_monthly_cost / (avg_pool_capacity_tokens_month)
- realized_price = list_price * (1 - average_discount - promo_credits_effect)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an exploratory sheet. Numbers are intentionally simple to keep scenario comparisons transparent.
- Please flag any conservative biases you prefer (eg bigger contractor bench vs faster hiring).
- Relevant tickets and data pulls are linked above.

End of sheet.
